title: Selective Disclosure of Hidden Directives in Reasoning Models: Behavioral Asymmetry and Steering
abstract: arXiv:2608.29070v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces are increasingly proposed as a mechanism for AI oversight: a monitor inspecting a model's reasoning can, in principle, detect misbehavior invisible from outputs alone. This assumes CoT surfaces what a model is instructed to do regardless of the instructions given. We test this assumption along two axes. First, we introduce the Instruction-Compliance Gap (ICG): the difference in probability that a model's CoT explicitly references a hidden system prompt directive when that directive is malign versus benign. Across 100 task pairs and 8 frontier reasoning models from 5 families, we find consistent asymmetric disclosure, a higher probability of leaking malign hidden instructions than benign ones, in Qwen3-14B (Wilcoxon $p=0.0001$, $+13.9$pp), Qwen3-32B ($p=0.0011$, $+13.0$pp), Qwen3-235B ($p=0.035$, $+5.8$pp), and similar results with MiniMax-M2.5 and DeepSeek-R1. The detector has 100% precision agains

translated_title: 推理模型中隐藏指令的选择性披露：行为不对称性与引导
translated_abstract: 思维链推理轨迹正日益被提议作为AI监督的一种机制：原则上，检查模型推理过程的监控器可以检测到仅从输出无法察觉的不当行为。这一假设假定：无论给定什么指令，思维链都会显现模型被指示去做的事情。我们沿两个维度检验这一假设。首先，我们提出“指令合规差距”（ICG）的概念：当隐藏的系统提示指令为恶意与为良性时，模型思维链明确引用该隐藏指令的概率之差。在100个任务对和来自5个系列的8个前沿推理模型上，我们一致观察到不对称披露现象——泄露恶意隐藏指令的概率高于良性指令——在Qwen3-14B（Wilcoxon p=0.0001，+13.9个百分点）、Qwen3-32B（p=0.0011，+13.0个百分点）、Qwen3-235B（p=0.035，+5.8个百分点）以及MiniMax-M2.5和DeepSeek-R1上均得到类似结果。该检测器具有100%的精确率……
tldr: 该论文提出“指令合规差距”（ICG）概念，发现推理模型的思维链会不对称地披露隐藏指令——泄露恶意指令的概率显著高于良性指令，从而对基于思维链的AI监督机制提出挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Instruction-Compliance Gap (ICG) and reveals that reasoning models asymmetrically disclose hidden directives in their chain-of-thought, leaking malign instructions at a significantly higher rate than benign ones, challenging CoT-based AI oversight.
